title: Light-sheet Fluorescence Microscopy for the Study of the Murine Heart
protocol: Retrieve a continuous wave laser with wavelengths of 405 nm, 473 nm, and 532 nm.
Place two mirrors (M1 and M2) 150 mm apart.
Align mirrors M1 and M2 at 45° to the beam.
Pass the beam through a 25-mm diameter iris diaphragm/pinhole.
Pass the beam through a 50-mm diameter neutral density filter with an optical density range of 0 - 4.0.
Expand the beam using a beam expander.
Pass the expanded beam through a 30 mm slit with a width of ~0 - 6 mm.
Reflect the beam off a mirror (M3) positioned at 45° to the beam.
Pass the beam through a 50:50 beam splitter placed 150 mm from M3.
Place mirror M6 150 mm from the beam splitter and align it at 45° to the forward-emitted beam.
Use the reflected beam from M6 to form one side of the dual-illumination light sheet.
Place mirror M4 150 mm from the beam splitter and align it at 45° to the beam emitted at a 90° angle.
Place second mirror M5 150 mm from M4 and align it at 45° to the reflected beam from M6.
Use the emitted beam from M5 to form the second side of the dual-illumination light sheet.
Set up the dual-sided illumination system symmetrically.
Place cylindrical lens CL1 [diameter = 1 in; focal length = 50 mm] 150 mm in line with the beam emitted from M5 on one side.
Place identical cylindrical lens CL2 150 mm in line with the beam emitted from M6 on the other side.
Place mirrors M7 and M8 each in line with the cylindrical lenses at distances of 50 mm to reflect the beams at 90°.
Form an achromatic doublet using two lenses, L1 (diameter = 1 in; focal length = 100 mm) and L2 (diameter = 1 in; focal length = 60 mm).
Place lens L1 100 mm from M7.
Place lens L2 160 mm from L1.
Repeat the process on the other side of the dual-illumination setup with identical lenses, L3 and L4, placed the same distance from M8.
Place mirrors M9 and M10, 60 mm from lenses L2 and L4 respectively, in line with the beam.
Place illumination objectives OL1 and OL2 (d = 2 in; f = 150 mm) 150 mm from M9 and M10 in line with the beam.
Embed a piece of cover glass [refractive index (RI) = 1.4745] on each side of the chamber, perpendicular to the illumination beam.
Install a stereo microscope with a 1X magnification objective and a scientific complementary metal oxide semiconductor (sCMOS) camera perpendicular to the illumination plane.
Retrieve fluorescent polystyrene beads that are 0.53 μm in diameter.
Dilute the bead solution in a refractive index matching solution (RIMS) with 1% low-melt pointing agarose to 1:150,000.
Cut a piece of borosilicate glass tubing with an inner diameter of 12 mm and an outer diameter of 18 mm to a length of 30 mm.
Mix the diluted bead sample with 1% agarose.
Pipette the bead/agarose solution into the borosilicate tubing.
Allow the agarose to solidify at room temperature (23 °C).
Fill the ABS chamber with a 99.5% glycerol solution.
Place the borosilicate glass tubing containing the beads inside the chamber.
Position the ABS chamber in the imaging system center of the Gaussian beam created by the dual illumination system.
Attach a 3-D motorized translational stage to the borosilicate glass tubing to control sample movement and orientation within the ABS chamber.
Acquire images using the sCMOS camera at a rate of 30 frames per second (fps).
Move the sample 1 mm in the lateral direction and acquire images at each 1-mm increment.
Continue imaging until the entire sample has been imaged.
Stack acquired images using visualization software.
Measure the point spread function (PSF) of the system using bead images.
Use this PSF for deconvolution during image processing in later steps.
Rinse the hearts in 1x phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) three times for 10 min each time.
Place the rinsed hearts in a 4% paraformaldehyde solution and incubate overnight at 4 °C.
Place the paraformaldehyde-fixed samples in a 4% acrylamide solution containing 0.5% w/v of 2,2’-Azobis dihydrochloride.
Incubate the samples at 4 °C overnight.
Remove the samples and incubate them at 37 °C for 2 - 3 hours.
Rinse the acrylamide-treated samples with PBS.
Place the rinsed samples in an 8% w/v sodium dodecyl sulfate solution containing 1.25% w/v boric acid.
Incubate the samples until they are clear, at 37 °C for several hours if necessary.
After clearing, place the samples in 1x phosphate-buffered saline for one day.
Prepare a refractive index matching solution with 40 g of nonionic density gradient medium and 30 mL of 0.02 M phosphate buffer (PB), adjusted to pH 7.5 with sodium hydroxide.
Add 0.1% Tween-20 and 0.01% sodium azide to the refractive index matching solution.
Place cleared samples in the refractive index matching solution with a refractive index of 1.46 - 1.48, along with 1% agarose.
Insert the sample into borosilicate glass tubing and allow the agarose to solidify at room temperature (23 °C).
Attach a 3-D motorized translational stage to the borosilicate glass tubing to control the movement and orientation of the sample within the 3-D printed ABS chamber.

Inject 8.7 x 10^12 viruses of type AAV9 containing a cardiac-specific troponin T promoter (cTnT) and green fluorescent protein (GFP) into the tail vein of a 2-month-old wild-type mouse in a 100-μL volume.
Dissect adult mouse hearts at 7.5 months of age.
Connect the motor controller to the motor actuator.
Attach the actuator to the borosilicate glass tubing to control the movement and orientation of the sample within the 3-D printed ABS chamber.
Position the sample so that it is in the center of the Gaussian beam created by the dual illumination system.
Acquire images using the sCMOS camera at a rate of 100 fps.
Move the sample 1 mm in the axial direction using the motor controller.
Acquire images with the sCMOS camera at each 1-mm increment.
Continue acquiring images until the entire sample has been imaged.
Stack the acquired images using a visualization software.
Develop 3-D images using these image stacks and the visualization software.
Deconvolve the PSF from step 2.6 with the acquired image stack.
Set a pixel threshold intensity value to observe the contours of the heart.
Add pseudo-color to the images based on this gray-scale intensity.
